paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar ben Perata. (a) Mishnah Gittin 3:4; Ta'anit, chapter 3, 19b. His sons Perata and Shimon (see there). He engaged in Torah and kindness, was arrested with his colleague Chananya ben Teradyon, and Elijah saved him. Five accusations were brought against him. Asked why he did not attend Bei Avidan, he said he was old and feared being trampled, Avodah Zarah 17b; see Shabbat 116a. He hinted to flee: “Ask Jacob, Moses, David”—they fled, Bamidbar Rabbah, beginning of section 23.

(b) Elazar Hammodai was his teacher, Sanhedrin, Kohen Gadol 22a; In Shevuat Ha'edut and Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 11 [1:9:4 in the checked edition], the reports are in Hammodai’s name [the Bavli names Elazar ben Azaryah and Chanina, Rabbi Yehoshua’s nephew]. Yuchasin, Rema’s Yesod Olam glosses, calls him Zakkai’s colleague, then nearby Rabbi’s colleague. Neither works. He reported his teacher Hammodai, Zakkai’s student. Even making Hammodai Zakkai’s colleague, Perata would not be Zakkai’s colleague. Certainly not Rabbi’s, much later. Shimon ben Elazar was Rabbi’s colleague and Elazar ben Perata spoke in his name. Yet both may be right: below there is another Elazar ben Perata, grandson of the earlier one; one could be in Zakkai’s time, one Rabbi’s. Shimon ben Elazar from Elazar ben Perata, in Hammodai’s name, Sanhedrin 22a. Tosefta, end of Sukkah: Elazar ben Perata and Eliezer ben Yaakov say, etc.; Abba Yose ben Chanan, etc.; Chananya ben Antigonus, etc.; Yehudah, etc.

(c) Reuben reincarnated in Elazar ben Perata: though opposing Joseph’s sale, through him they threw Joseph into the pit. Thus Moses’ “Let Reuben live and not die” prayed for his rescue in that incarnation, Emek Hammelekh, 39c. See Eliezer ben Hyrcanus, Reuben’s reincarnation.
